name: Dimitrov cube-free: lower branch theta*(c) = (c+3)/5 on (1, 7/6]
comment: Companion to dimitrov_cubefree.json, identical region, slices on the lower branch. Binding set {tail_S2, h_average, vdC_q0_via_S9}, attained at zeta = eta = (4c-3)/5. See the main file for the full transcription notes.

provenance.tail_S2: Section 6, displays (50)-(54): S^(2)_c(x) << x^{c+eps} z^{-1}, via the two divisor-counting bounds x^c T^{-2} and x^c D^{-2} with DT > z/4.
provenance.h_average: Display (38), first term x^c H^{-1} d^{-3} t^{-3} with H = x^eta/(dt), giving x^{c-eta}(dt)^{-2}; the sum over dt <= z converges.
provenance.vdC_q0: Display (38), second term x^{1/2} H^{1/2}: Lemma 2 at q = 0. With H = x^eta/(dt) this is x^{(1+eta)/2}(dt)^{-1/2}, and sum_{n<=z} tau(n) n^{-1/2} << z^{1/2+eps} contributes zeta/2. Here F ~ h x again, by (33) and (36).
provenance.vdC_q0_via_S9: Displays (44)-(47): S^(6) << x^{1-c} S^(9) with Lemma 2 at q = 0, giving x^{(3-2c)/2} H^{3/2}(dt)^{-3/2}; the sum converges.
provenance.dropped_third: Display (38), third term x^{c-1} H^{-1} t^{-3} log^2 x. The paper absorbs it into the first term, which requires d^3 <= x, i.e. zeta <= 1/3, false for every c > 7/6 at the paper's own zeta = (2c-1)/4. It is RETAINED here. With H = x^eta/(dt) it is x^{c-1-eta} d t^{-2}, and sum_{dt<=z} d t^{-2} ~ z^2 (the d-sum diverges), giving exponent c - 1 + 2 zeta - eta.
